newsitem.title: UK: Mideast tankers steady, inter-U.K./Cont firms.
newsitem.headline: Mideast tankers steady, inter-U.K./Cont firms.

text.p: Middle East crude tanker rates remained steady while the inter-U.K./Cont market was the main sector to show a marked increase on Friday, brokers said.

U.K./Cont 80,000 tonners firmed to W115/117.5 from W105 on Thursday. "There's a lot of activity and a lack of tonnage, especially for the end of January," one broker said. "It could move up a bit more next week."
Brokers said a pipeline problem on Teesside could cause delays next week, but no vessels had been cancelled so far.
They said demand from the Middle East/West was emerging more clearly than earlier in the week, with very large crude carriers still at around W55.
Brokers E.A. Gibson said virtually all sectors had firmed in the last week and there were "indications of this firmer trend continuing in the near future."
From the Middle East, they expect 61 very large and ultra-large crude carriers amounting to about 18.3 million tonnes being available within the next four weeks.
Mideast-Singapore rates for VLCCs were steady at W57.5 and to Japan at W67.5.
Million-barrel vessels from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf edged up to W95 from W92.5, with VLCCs steady at W62.5. "West Africa million barrels are firming all the time," one broker said.
Transatlantic million-barrel rates were little changed at W95, with VLCCs at a steady W62.5.

Cross-Med rates were likewise flat at W100 for 80,000 tonners and W87.5 for million barrel ships. "The Med market could get a bit of help next week from West Africa which has been rising steadily," an Italian broker said.
On fuel oil, 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont was seen done at W200, up about five points. "There are a lot of Baltic cargoes around," one broker said.
Brokers said the Caribbean remained strong, with 70,000 tonners Caribs/upcoast at a steady W170-175. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
